mission.title: wasmedge-runtime: LFX Workspace: Memory alignment in WASM instructions
mission.description: LFX Workspace: Memory alignment in WASM instructions. Community-reported issue about misaligned typed pointers in WASI host functions.

steps.title: Reproduce the misaligned pointer trap
steps.description:
Run the WasmEdge regression or local sample that triggers a misaligned typed pointer so you can capture the current failure mode.
```bash
wasmedge --version
wasmedge tests/wasm/misaligned_pointer.wasm
```
The bad behavior to confirm is `__WASI_ERRNO_ADDRNOTAVAIL` instead of `ErrCode::UnalignedAtomicAccess`.

steps.title: Inspect the affected host functions
steps.description:
Search the runtime sources for the typed-pointer handling in the args/env and clock host functions.
```bash
git grep -n 'ADDRNOTAVAIL\|UnalignedAtomicAccess\|typed pointer' .
```
Use the matches to verify where the misalignment trap is being downgraded.

steps.title: Apply the fix for LFX Workspace: Memory alignment in WASM instructions
Verify the misalignment fix
steps.description:
Run the targeted regression tests and confirm the misaligned-pointer case now traps with the expected error.
```bash
cargo test -p wasmedge-wasi
wasmedge tests/wasm/misaligned_pointer.wasm
```
Check that the old `__WASI_ERRNO_ADDRNOTAVAIL` path no longer appears.

resolution.summary: This is a follow-up to #5089. The fix extends the same WASI typed pointer misalignment trap behavior to the args/env and clock host functions, so misaligned pointers now fail fast with `ErrCode::UnalignedAtomicAccess` instead of being misreported as `__WASI_ERRNO_ADDRNOTAVAIL`. That keeps the runtime behavior consistent across WASI imports and avoids masking alignment bugs.

prerequisites.description: A working wasmedge-runtime installation or development environment.
